kill_fact: The record was written on 4 August 2026 BEFORE Emerson's fiscal-Q3 2026 print, and it pre-registered its own falsification tests: 'What confirms the bear: gross margin down again year over year on tonight's print; a full-year underlying growth guide cut below 3%; ... or an order rate that falls below the sales rate.' The print landed that evening (10-Q accepted 2026-08-04 16:07) and failed all three. (1) GROSS MARGIN EXPANDED, not contracted: $2,655m on $4,873m = 54.48%, against $2,393m on $4,553m = 52.56% in the June-2025 quarter, +192bps; stripping the $82m of tariff refunds the CFO said were booked in cost of sales still leaves 52.80%, +24bps year over year. The pricing-power read is affirmatively positive, not neutral: price contributed 3 points to growth and the CFO stated 'price cost certainly remains green' with 'price cost and cost reductions more than offset inflation' - which directly refutes the bear's core inference that rising revenue on flat gross margin is 'volume sold at the market price, not pricing power.' (2) GUIDANCE WAS RAISED, not cut: full-year underlying growth to 3.5% (GAAP 5%), adjusted EPS to ~$6.55, free cash flow to ~$3.6bn. (3) ORDERS still led sales (+7% vs +6% underlying). Worse for the bear, its two most quantified pillars inverted. The Middle East was OVER-provisioned, not under-provisioned: against the one point of full-year sales provisioned in May 2026, the actual Q3 impact was '$25 million' with Q4 'similar' and the full-year effect 'approximately $100 million... approximately 0.5 point of revenue,' with field service engineers back 'at pre-conflict levels.' And the project funnel is not flat at $11.2bn 'consumed by conversions' - it 'grew $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion, up 8% year-over-year,' with the power funnel +$450m to $3.0bn and the LNG funnel +$350m to $2.2bn. Backlog is $8.2bn, up 7% (the record's $7.4bn is stale). Every one of the three deductions building the $97 adverse case is contradicted by dated primary evidence from the company itself.
corrections: FOUR corrections, three of which move numbers. (1) NET DEBT - load-bearing input to both valuation levels. The record subtracts $12.27bn 'at 31 March 2026'; that figure verifies exactly against the Q2 balance sheet ($14,057m total debt less $1,791m cash = $12,266m), but it is now stale. At 30 June 2026 total debt is $13,113m against $2,180m of cash = $10,933m, a $1.33bn reduction in one quarter on $1.3bn of Q3 free cash flow (+36% year over year, 27.1% margin). Carried through the record's own base bridge ($95.2bn enterprise value, 558m diluted shares), base fair value moves $148 -> $151. (2) ADVERSE CASE - the sop_bear takes EBITDA from $5.2bn to $4.75bn via three deductions, all three now falsified by the 4 Aug 2026 disclosure: -$180m for the Middle East running at 50% capacity (actual full-year impact ~$100m of revenue, ~$30m EBITDA at the record's own 30% incremental - restore $150m); -$188m for a one-point gross-margin give-back to copper and freight (price +3 points, price-cost 'green' - restore $188m); -$60m for a test-and-measurement reversion as a 'distributor restocking pulse' (T&M sales +23%, orders +19%, semiconductor orders +70%, full-year T&M guide RAISED to +14% - restore $60m). Adverse EBITDA becomes $5.15bn; holding the record's OWN 14.1x de-rate multiple gives an enterprise value of $72.6bn, and carrying the record's own +$0.33bn adverse net-debt premium over actual net debt gives $11.3bn, so equity is $61.3bn across 562m shares = $109. bear_px moves $97 -> $109. (3) STALE OPERATING FACTS, non-numeric: backlog is $8.2bn up 7% (record: '$7.4 billion... up 9%'); the funnel is $12.4bn up 8% (record: 'flat at about $11.2 billion across five quarters'); the '$350m of LNG in a $7.4bn backlog, under 5%' figure is a November-2025 datapoint the record applies to an August-2026 book in which the LNG funnel alone is $2.2bn and up 19%. (4) WHAT SURVIVES, and it is not nothing - the returns and balance-sheet critique verifies against the 30 June 2026 sheet and is untouched by one quarter: goodwill $18,122m plus intangibles $8,686m = $26,808m of $42,208m total assets (63.5%, the record's '64%' is right), tangible book value is negative $6.43bn, the current ratio is 0.90, and $5,587m of the debt is short-term. Two honest hedges on the print itself: the headline gross-margin expansion is flattered by the $82m tariff refund in cost of sales (management excluded it from adjusted), and the cash beat was helped by that refund plus tax payments the CFO said shifted from Q3 into Q4. Book-to-bill was exactly 1.0 in the quarter (not above 1) and backlog growth decelerated from 9% to 7% - the bear's only surviving score, and a thin one.
